title: R' Shimon bar Chuta

paragraphs: Bereshit Rabbah 26:3 cites a homily of his: he said that, according to the numerical value of the letters of Shem’s name, the Holy One, blessed be He, granted the generations respite from the Flood until the Dispersion: three hundred and forty years.
He may be the one mentioned under the name Bar Chatya.

notes.text: The source parenthesis של שם is ambiguous here; the referent of shem and the precise wording of the numerical explanation remain unresolved. The cited paragraph was not located in the bounded check. The number 340 and the possible Bar Chatya connection are retained.

The saved whole TE BereshitRabbah26:3 paragraph begins with Noah’s sons, then Shimon bar Chutah’s340-year respite. Thus שם refers to Shem, whose shin300 plus mem40 explains the number, rather than an unspecified divine Name. Supplied24:3 and heading Chuta versus named Chutah remain distinct; the match is not printed dalet/vav history proof. The paragraph supplies no full Rabbi title for Shimon. Bar Chatya remains Hyman’s possible identification with its hedge, not a new authority merge.

The print (vol. III, p. 1174) gives Bereshit Rabbah 26:3, where the supplied Hebrew transcription gives 24:3. The passage at 26:3 names Noah’s son Shem before the saying attributed to Shimon bar Chutah. The numerical value of Shem’s name is 340 (shin 300 plus mem 40). The heading spells Chuta, and Hyman offers the connection to Bar Chatya as a possibility.
